newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Audi considers car assembly in Macedonia.
newsitem.headline: Audi considers car assembly in Macedonia.

text.p: Audi AG, part of the German automotive group Volkswagen AG, said on Friday it was considering assembling cars in Macedonia.
"We are studying the feasibility of building kits of Audi cars in Macedonia," a company spokesman, Jurgen DeGraeve, told Reuters.
"We are considering different models and different volumes of production, but there have been no major decisions," DeGraeve said.
A decision on assembling cars in the Balkan nation, formerly a part of Yugoslavia, will depend on prospects for exporting to neighbouring countries, he said.
"We are looking to see whether we could supply other countries from Macedonia," he said. "We are investigating the tariffs and trade regulations in the region."
DeGraeve declined to comment on recent reports that Audi has agreed to build its A3 cars through a joint venture with the Macedonian government.
"We won't talk about any details until we know them," he said. "It's still too early, and any figures could change from week to week."
DeGraeve spoke at the Audi engine plant in Gyor in western Hungary. The plant is being expanded to build Audi's new TT cars beginning in the second quarter of 1998, he said.
